clue.text: Job taken by schoolteacher who is responsible for local deliveries?

definitions.text: who is responsible for local deliveries?

parts.note: a job or position is a post
a mistress is an old word for a female schoolteacher, as in 'maths mistress'

explanation.surface: A teacher takes on a second job delivering the local mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by description: the woman in charge of a local post office handles the area's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: She runs a local post office, from which the neighbourhood's mail goes out.

clue.text: Marjoram leaves are no go for cooking

indicators.note: cooking suggests ingredients being worked over, so the letters of the phrase are mixed up

explanation.surface: A herb's leaves are said to be off-limits in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' rearranges ARE NO GO into the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb sold under this name is wild marjoram, whose dried leaves are used in Italian dishes.

clue.text: Farm vehicle lifted up on it transformed pulling power

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up reads it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle

indicators.note: transformed tells us the two little words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tractor is hoisted and reworked to give it more hauling strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted up' turns CART into TRAC, and 'transformed' rearranges ON IT into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the grip or force with which something is pulled along, as a locomotive hauls a train.

clue.text: One met up with such a romantic couple

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone met their sweetheart and they became a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the word for met from the bottom in this down clue; 'item' is informal for a couple who are dating.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people dating are called an item in informal speech.

clue.text: Drivers can opt for this insurance: 33⅓ do

definitions.text: Drivers can opt for this insurance

parts.note: thirty-three and a third per cent is one third of a whole
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Motorists choose a basic insurance policy, with a puzzling figure attached.
explanation.walkthrough: British motor insurance at its most basic level covers only damage to other people, known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the minimum British car cover, protecting other road users rather than the policyholder.

clue.text: Putting oneself in that position is to some extent mischievous

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Putting yourself in someone else's shoes is a little naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' takes the letters inside onesELF IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are imps of folklore, so elfin behaviour is impish and playful.

clue.text: Skis with ace all over the place but not well on water

indicators.note: something all over the place is in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An ace water-skier wobbles about and feels unwell on the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges SKIS and ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling nauseous on a boat is the motion sickness of sailors.

clue.text: Lady member of US legislature shows female sex is in front

indicators.note: this says the word for sex comes before the word for female

parts.note: congress is a formal word for sexual intercourse
a woman is a female person

explanation.surface: A female legislator shows women leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in front' puts the word for sex first. That word also names the US legislature, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: A female member of the US House of Representatives is called this.

clue.text: Friend gets behind general feeling in a spectacular way

indicators.note: the friend comes after, at the end of the word for feeling

parts.note: a sensation is a feeling, a general awareness through the senses
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend supports the general's mood in a showy fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer but just describes the feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done sensationally is done in a dramatic, thrilling manner.

clue.text: Perform Carmen perhaps in front of empty theatre

indicators.note: the word for Carmen comes before the remaining letters

parts.note: Carmen is an opera by Bizet, an example of the form

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A company stages Bizet's opera to an empty house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves TE from theatre, its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or work, as a machine performs its task.

clue.text: Blow up trendy apartment facing east

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
flat is the British word for an apartment

explanation.surface: A fashionable east-facing apartment explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' reads as destruction, but it means pump up.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate a balloon or tyre is to fill it with air.

clue.text: 18th President's financial help for students

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ... was the eighteenth President of the United States
money given towards a student's education

explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant held the US presidency eighteenth in line, and a sum awarded to fund study shares his surname.

clue.text: Tissue at back of throat and nose, I add, is abnormal

indicators.note: abnormal means not in its usual form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor notes something odd about a patient's throat and nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is abnormal' rearranges NOSE and I ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lymph glands at the back of the nasal cavity, often removed from children.

clue.text: Concorde captain, say, with little luggage but a small electric indicator

parts.note: the captain of an aircraft such as Concorde is its pilot
travelling light means carrying little luggage

explanation.surface: A Concorde captain packs light and notices a little warning lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling light' means carrying few bags, so 'with little luggage' gives LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lamp that shows a device is switched on goes by this name.

clue.text: Green Engineering Company reasonable?

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for engineering
logical means sensible or reasonable

explanation.surface: Asks whether an environmentally friendly engineering firm is sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a colour but is the environmental sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in politics means caring for the environment, the concern of the science of habitats.

clue.text: Satirical piece in second gear

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A comic sketch set in a car changing into second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' looks like a car's gear but means equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch mocking something is a skit.

clue.text: Worn by strippers, tuned by violinists

definitions.meaning: a skimpy undergarment of a thin strip of cloth
the lowest string on a violin is tuned to the note G

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny thong a stripper wears, and the violin's lowest-pitched cord tuned to G, share the name.

clue.text: Therefore twice is average

indicators.note: twice says the word is written two times

parts.note: so means therefore

explanation.surface: A logical step repeated is merely middling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre or unremarkable is called so-so.

clue.text: Is verbally aggressive on the pitch and toboggans

definitions.text: Is verbally aggressive on the pitch
definitions.meaning: in cricket, sledging is insulting a batsman to put them off
sleighs for sliding down snowy slopes

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a fielder who taunts the batsman is said to sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang for taunting an opponent and the plural of small sleighs share the same spelling.

clue.text: So firm is to broadcast very loud music

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A determined DJ insists on playing music at top volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SO FIRM IS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction, Italian for very strong, marks a passage played very loudly.

clue.text: M/1000 + Gaelic = flood

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1000, so M over 1000 is one, I, written before the two thousands, M and M
Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: A mathematical equation in which a fraction plus a language equals a deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written as a sum: the fraction gives I (1000 divided by 1000 is one) followed by M and M for the two thousands, and the plus sign joins ERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse something is to plunge it fully under liquid, as a flood submerges land.

clue.text: Bid higher for deliveries by telephone

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
to call is to telephone

explanation.surface: A firm makes a higher offer for home deliveries ordered by phone.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled in a row, each called a delivery; 'Bid' is a bridge term.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, to make a bid above the opponent's previous one is to overcall.

clue.text: Pepper-sounds like Santiago country

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the answer is spoken the same as the country

parts.note: Santiago is the capital of Chile

explanation.surface: Peppers are said to come from the South American nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' gives the spelling of the hot pepper from the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot pepper used in cooking is a chilli, here spelt the American way.

clue.text: Strum balalaikas to provide ambience for this dance

indicators.note: ambience surrounds something, so the words around contain the answer

explanation.surface: Musicians play balalaikas to set the mood for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide ambience for' points to the letters inside stRUM BAlalaikas.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance of Cuban origin is a rumba.

clue.text: In Sicily gives rise to lava and in France, sodium

definitions.text: In Sicily gives rise to lava

parts.note: et is French for and
Na is the chemical symbol of sodium

explanation.surface: Compares lava-flows in Sicily with sodium in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of the Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe's highest active volcano stands in Sicily and erupts molten rock.

clue.text: Doing it one might catch a no good fish

parts.note: ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler might catch a worthless fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the activity: while doing it, you may catch something.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with rod and line is angling, a pastime aimed at catches.

clue.text: Move to Rhyl they say: it's leafy, twisty and upwardly mobile

definitions.text: it's leafy, twisty and upwardly mobile

parts.note: to tend is to move or incline in a direction

indicators.note: they say indicates a word spoken aloud, giving its sound

parts.note: Rhyl is a seaside town in north Wales, pronounced to rhyme with 'pill'

explanation.surface: A move to a Welsh resort is described as a social climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' gives RIL, the sound of RHYL, a resort town on the north Wales coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant's thin coiling shoot grips supports and grows upward.

clue.text: Wear this skirt, lose a kilo, change into dress with tai lered bodice

indicators.note: lose means the letter for kilo is taken out of the phrase
change into says the remaining letters turn into a new arrangement

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for kilo

explanation.surface: Slim down a little and swap a skirt for a smart fitted dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' removes K from WEAR THIS SKIRT and 'change into' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress with a shirt-like fitted top and buttoned front goes by this name.
